articles.title: 'No Loyalty To Pak?': Khawaja Asif Sounds Alarm Over Bureaucrats' Exodus To US, Canada, Europe
articles.description: Pakistan may be sinking, and the first to sense it may be its own elite. Defence Minister Khawaja Asif has raised the alarm over what he calls a bureaucratic exodus, accusing senior officers of arranging to settle in Canada, the United States, Britain and Europe while still serving the state. He singled out Portugal, claiming influential officials have prepared their families and finances for relocation, and asked whether they are truly loyal to Pakistan or merely in transit. It is not his first charge: in August 2025, he alleged that over half of the senior bureaucracy had bought property or sought citizenship there. Meanwhile, GDP growth is 3.65 percent, external debt is 137.55 billion dollars and reserves cover two months of imports. The government has published no verified list of those allegedly leaving. Responding to Union Minister Kiren Rijiju’s remarks about CJP, Nawaz called his claims baseless and urged Prime Minister Narendra Modi to demonstrate India’s commitment to democracy by protecting dissent and addressing protesters’ concerns. articles.title: 'Paris Will Turn Muslim Soon': Trump Blames Immigration For France Riots; Macron Blames Iran War
articles.description: Paris is on fire, and Donald Trump has turned France's unrest into an immigration battle. Trump tells Emmanuel Macron he should have closed his borders, claiming Paris will be a Muslim city very soon. Macron has a very different explanation: rising fuel prices, a cost-of-living crisis and the fallout of the war in Iran. Around 200,000 people joined protests, including nearly 40,000 in Paris, and about 2,400 were arrested over the weekend. Cars burned, shops were looted and a historic city hall was engulfed in flames. French authorities blame far-left radicals and criminal groups, while student groups and Yellow Vest activists plan more protests under the slogan Macron must go. So is France burning because of migration, or because people can no longer afford to live? Here is everything you need to know. Watch the story and tell us what you think in the comments. articles.title: US Attacks Iran Again! American Strike Hits Konarak Naval Base, Wounds 2 Iranian Soldiers
articles.description: Iran says American forces have carried out a fresh strike on its territory, targeting the Konarak naval base on the country’s southeastern coast and wounding two Iranian servicemen. According to Iran’s Navy, the US military used “two light projectiles” against the facility in Sistan and Baluchestan province, targeting a 35mm naval cannon. The Iranian account indicates the immediate damage was limited, but the location gives the incident wider significance. Konarak sits near Chabahar on the Gulf of Oman, east of the Strait of Hormuz. Iran recently announced an expanded naval deployment posture stretching from Hormuz into the Gulf of Oman and Arabian Sea, while warning that it intends to push American naval forces farther from its coastline. Tehran has also repeatedly warned that renewed US attacks could trigger retaliation against American forces and interests across the region.
